title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout this part Grothendieck works with a group 𝔊 (and its profinite completion), with a subgroup of index 2 written 𝔊^+. Consistent with the relations on this page, 𝔊^+ is SL2(Z) (or its completion), the orbifold fundamental group of M_{1,1}, and 𝔊 is the GL2-type extension containing an orientation-reversing involution τ. Inside it, Π is the level-2 congruence subgroup Γ(2) = μ × Π0, where μ = {±1} and Π0 is the free group on two generators, the fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞} (generated by the loops l_0, l_1, l_∞). The page is a finite-group computation inside this setup.

Step 1, relations (30). On the previous page (28) gives 𝔊/Π0 by generators ρ, σ, τ with τ(ρ)=ρ and τ(σ)=σ^{-1}. Grothendieck changes to a new involution τ'; τ' = τσ fits all the relations. He gets the presentation ρ^6 = σ^4 = τ'^2 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2, τ'ρτ'^{-1} = ρ^{-1}, τ'στ'^{-1} = σ^{-1}, σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}.

Step 2, relations (31). The index-2 subgroup 𝔊^+/Π0 = ⟨ρ, σ | ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2, σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}⟩. This is the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group Dic_3 ≅ Z/3 ⋊ Z/4 of order 12, i.e. SL2(Z)/F2. Its central element ρ^3 = σ^2 = −1 generates μ.

Step 3, the question asked. How does M_{0,3}^~ ≃ M/±1 act on this group? Here M is the automorphism group cut out by the 'équation des lacets', a GT-type group. Grothendieck uses the central extension (32): 1 → μ → 𝔊^+/Π0 → 𝔊^+/Π ≅ S_3 → 1. The automorphisms in question preserve this extension structure.

Step 4, the classification. Elements of M^!/±1 induce the identity on the quotient S_3 and on μ. An automorphism of a central extension that is trivial on both kernel and quotient has the form x ↦ c(x̄)·x with c ∈ Hom(S_3, μ) = Hom(S_3^{ab}, ±1). So this automorphism group is Z/2, and its generator is Θ(x) = sg(x)·x, where sg is the sign character pulled back through S_3. Hence Θ(ρ) = ρ (ρ maps to a 3-cycle) and Θ(σ) = −σ = σ^{-1} (σ maps to a transposition).

What it serves. On the next page this gives u|_{𝔊^+/Π0} = Θ^{ε_2(u)}, i.e. the commutator [u̇, σ̇] = ε_2(u). So ε_2 is a ±1-valued character of the group M, read off from its action on the order-12 quotient Dic_3 of π_1^orb(M_{1,1}). The surrounding goal is to show that the elements u of the centralizer-type group Z_{ρ,σ} come from M_{0,3}^~, i.e. to compare the 'Teichmüller' group of the genus-1 / level-2 tower with the genus-0 one.
errors: No mathematical error. Θ is a genuine outer automorphism: an inner automorphism inducing the identity on S_3 (which has trivial center) is conjugation by an element of μ, hence trivial. So the group of such automorphisms is indeed Z/2, with Θ(σ) = −σ = σ^{-1}.
Gap, presentational only: the passage from τ to τ' is not stated on the page. τ' = τσ is consistent with (28) ⇒ (30): τ'ρτ'^{-1} = ρ^{-1}, τ'στ'^{-1} = σ^{-1} and τ'^2 = 1 all check.
The notation x ↦ −σ silently writes μ = {±1} multiplicatively inside the group, so −σ means ρ^3σ = σ^3.

ideas.what: Presentation of SL2(Z)/F2 (quotient of SL2(Z) by the free part of Γ(2)) as the dicyclic group of order 12, and the corresponding order-24 quotient of the GL2 version with an extra involution τ'
ideas.modern_name: binary dihedral group Dic_3 = Z/3 ⋊ Z/4 as a central extension of S_3 = SL2(Z/2) by ±1

ideas.what: Automorphisms of a central extension trivial on kernel and quotient are classified by Hom(quotient, kernel); here Hom(S_3, ±1) = Z/2, with generator x ↦ sg(x)x
ideas.modern_name: automorphisms of central extensions / 1-cocycles (Hom(G,A) for central A)

ideas.what: Defining a sign character ε_2 on the 'Teichmüller/GT-type' group M by its action on the finite quotient Dic_3 of π_1(M_{1,1}) ([u, σ] = ε_2(u))
ideas.modern_name: a ±1-valued character of a GT-type group / Galois action on π_1^orb(M_{1,1}) detected at level 2 (related to the cyclotomic character mod 4, i.e. Q(i))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Galois actions on π_1(M_{1,1}) studied by Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Lochak–Schneps (1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the genus-0/genus-1 Teichmüller tower in general terms only

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine finite-group computation (a presentation of Dic_3 and the Hom(S_3, ±1) classification of extension automorphisms). It serves a larger, known program: comparing the GT-type group across the genus 0 and genus 1 / level-2 towers. Nothing here is new or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The group is written with a fraktur G (𝔊^+/Π0, 𝔊^+/Π), consistent with the neighbouring pages, not 𝔖^+/π_0; S_3 is the symmetric group 𝔖_3.
In (30), σ(ρ) = ρ^{-1} and τ'(ρ) = ρ^{-1} denote conjugation (σρσ^{-1}, etc.).
Line 6, '(31)': the presentation is in ρ, σ, enclosed in braces, as transcribed.
Archive page number at the bottom left is 579.
